# Non-HTML responses return empty PreviewResult (not PARSE_ERROR)

Governing standard: `e4c48c87-e4ef-4b91-9fad-98eedbdd80c1` (Fetch Safety &
Resilience) — "Accept `text/html` responses; skip clearly non-HTML content types
without erroring (return empty fields)."

## Problem
`fetch.ts` `fetchDocument` already returns `{ url, html: "", contentType }` when
`!isHtmlContentType(contentType)` (e.g. `application/pdf`, `application/json`).
But `preview.ts` `extractPreview` treats `html === ""` as an error:
```
if (fetched.html === "") {
  throw new PreviewError("PARSE_ERROR", `No HTML content at ${rawUrl}`, { url });
}
```
Result: a non-HTML URL maps to `PARSE_ERROR` → HTTP 502. The standard requires
an empty-fields result, not an error.

## Recommended approach
Distinguish "empty because non-HTML" from a genuine parse failure:
1. In `extractPreview`, branch on the fetch outcome BEFORE cheerio.load:
   - If `fetched.html === ""` AND content type is non-HTML (or missing),
     return a valid empty PreviewResult directly:
     ```
     { url: fetched.url, title: "", description: "",
       adapter: "default", fetchedAt: Date.now(), fromCache: false }
     ```
     (no image/siteName — omitted per Output Contract). Do NOT throw.
   - Keep the `PARSE_ERROR` throw ONLY for an actual `cheerio.load` failure
     (the existing try/catch) — that is a true parse error.
2. Optional refinement: thread an explicit flag (e.g. add `nonHtml?: boolean`
   to `FetchResult`) instead of string-matching `contentType`, so the contract
   between fetch and preview is explicit. Preferred for clarity; keep
   `contentType` plumbing as the source of truth either way.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A mocked fetch returning `Content-Type: application/pdf` (and an empty or
      binary body) yields a 200 PreviewResult with `title: ""`, `description: ""`,
      correct `url`/`fetchedAt`/`fromCache:false`, `adapter: "default"`, and NO
      `image`/`siteName` keys. Add this case to `preview.test.ts`.
- [ ] Same for `application/json`.
- [ ] A real HTML body that cheerio fails to parse STILL throws `PARSE_ERROR`
      (regression test already in place — keep it green).
- [ ] `preview()` never throws `PARSE_ERROR` solely due to a non-HTML content
      type.
- [ ] HTTP server maps the non-HTML case to 200 (covered by existing
      `_setPreviewFn` mock pattern if needed; no new server route logic).

## Affected surfaces
`packages/core/src/preview.ts` (primary), optionally `packages/core/src/types.ts`
(`FetchResult.nonHtml?`) and `fetch.ts` (set the flag), `preview.test.ts` (new
cases). No server changes.

## Rollback
Single-file revert of the `extractPreview` early-return branch.

## Risks
- Low. The only behavior change: non-HTML URLs go from 502 → 200 empty result,
  which is exactly what the standard mandates.
- Ensure cache still stores the empty result keyed by URL (current cache path is
  unchanged — empty result is a valid PreviewResult).

content.raw: # Built-in adapters resolve image URLs to absolute Governing standards: - `55d564d2-6fd1-4a7f-bb2d-a27a3b2aef37` (PreviewResult Output Contract) — "`image.url` must be an absolute URL (resolve relative URLs against the page base)." - `cf5fd7c7-f7bf-4e1a-8499-96571d087d58` (Adapter Authoring) — checklist item 2: "Resolve all returned URLs to absolute (use the page base)." ## Problem `extractors/default.ts` already resolves image/first-`` URLs to absolute via a private `resolveUrl(raw, base)` + `resolveBase($, url)` pair. But the two built-in adapters return raw attribute values: - `adapters/youtube.ts`: `image: { url: ogImage }` (raw). - `adapters/twitter.ts`: `image: { url: ogImage }` (raw). If a YouTube/Twitter page serves a relative `og:image` (e.g. `/assets/thumb.jpg` or `//cdn.../img.jpg`), the contract is violated. OG images are usually absolute today, but the standard is unconditional. ## Recommended approach 1. Extract the URL-resolution helpers from `extractors/default.ts` into a shared module, e.g. `packages/core/src/extractors/url.ts` exporting: - `resolveBase($, url: URL): URL` - `resolveUrl(raw: string, base: URL): string | undefined` Re-import them in `extractors/default.ts` to avoid duplication. 2. In both `youtube.ts` and `twitter.ts`, resolve the chosen image against the page base before returning: ``` const base = resolveBase($, ctx.url); const image = ogImage ? resolveUrl(ogImage, base) : undefined; ... ...(image ? { image: { url: image } } : {}) ``` Note: `AdapterContext.$` is typed `CheerioRoot = unknown` and cast to `CheerioAPI` inside adapters; `resolveBase` takes `CheerioAPI`, so pass the same cast (`ctx.$ as CheerioAPI`) — consistent with existing adapter code. 3. Adapters currently resolve base from `ctx.url` only (they ignore ``). For parity with the default extractor, use `resolveBase($, ctx.url)` which honors `` when present. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `youtube.test.ts`: add/extend a fixture where `og:image` is relative (`/vi/.../default.jpg`) and assert the returned `image.url` is absolute and on the correct origin. - [ ] `twitter.test.ts`: same with a relative `twitter:image`. - [ ] Absolute image URLs are passed through unchanged (idempotent resolution). - [ ] Protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.../x.jpg`) resolve to `https://cdn.../x.jpg` against the page base. - [ ] Malformed/unresolvable image URLs are dropped (no `image` field) rather than thrown — matches "return null to defer, never throw". - [ ] `extractors/default.ts` continues to resolve correctly after the refactor (its existing tests stay green). ## Affected surfaces New `packages/core/src/extractors/url.ts`; `extractors/default.ts` (import from new module); `adapters/youtube.ts`; `adapters/twitter.ts`; `youtube.test.ts`; `twitter.test.ts`. No server or public-API signature change. ## Rollback Inline revert per file; the helper extraction is the only structural change. ## Risks - Low. `resolveUrl`/`resolveBase` already exist and are tested via the default extractor; this reuses them. - Ensure `AdapterContext.$` cast stays consistent; do not re-parse HTML inside adapters (purity invariant from Adapter Authoring standard).

# Source-resolution export condition for @metascan/core (CRITICAL)

Governing standard: `0057ec32-0216-49ab-bf1b-c50370b730b4` (Metascan Runtime &
Toolchain) — "apps run directly from source — no `dist/` required" + Enforcement
gate (CI runs lint + typecheck + test).

## Problem
`packages/core/package.json` exports only `./dist/*`:
```
"exports": { ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js" } }
```
`dist/` is git-ignored and unbuildable in CI (no `build` step). `apps/server`
depends on core via `workspace:*`, so from a clean clone:
- `bun run typecheck` → TS2307 Cannot find module '@metascan/core' (server).
- server `*.test.ts` → error: Cannot find module '@metascan/core'.
Verified: building core → typecheck clean, 96/96 tests pass. Pure resolution gap.

## Recommended approach (source export condition)
1. `packages/core/package.json` — add a source condition ahead of `dist`:
   ```
   "exports": {
     ".": {
       "types": "./src/index.ts",
       "development": "./src/index.ts",
       "import": "./dist/index.js",
       "default": "./dist/index.js"
     }
   }
   ```
   Keep `main`/`module`/`files:["dist"]` as-is. `types` → source is fine because
   `src/index.ts` is the source of truth and tsc (Bundler) reads `.ts` directly.
2. Resolution wiring (must cover BOTH Bun runtime and tsc):
   - **tsc:** add `"customConditions": ["development"]` to the SHARED
     `tsconfig.json` (root) so all three typecheck configs apply it. Verify
     `tsc -p apps/server/tsconfig.json` resolves core to `src/index.ts`.
   - **Bun:** confirm `bun test` resolves the `development` condition. If Bun
     does not apply `development` by default, instead point a `"bun"` condition
     (which Bun always sets) at `./src/index.ts` for runtime, while keeping the
     `development`+`customConditions` path for tsc. (Decide via a 1-line probe:
     `bun -e "console.log(require.resolve('@metascan/core'))"` after the change.)
3. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — leave sequence as install→lint→typecheck→test
   (NO build step added). This is the acceptance gate.
4. Root `package.json` — the `typecheck` script is unchanged (three tsc -p
   invocations); confirm it still passes after the tsconfig edit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] From a clean checkout (delete `packages/core/dist`, `rm -rf node_modules`,
      `bun install`): `bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun test` ALL green.
- [ ] 96/96 tests pass; server test file runs fully (12 tests), no module error.
- [ ] `bun pack` in `packages/core` produces a tarball whose `exports`/`types`
      still resolve to `dist/` (publish contract unchanged). Inspect the packed
      `package.json` to confirm `development`/source entries are harmless to
      external consumers (they resolve to `src` only under the condition, which
      npm installs do not activate).
- [ ] No `build` step added to CI.
- [ ] Biome lint stays clean (no new violations from package.json/tsconfig edits).

## Affected surfaces
`packages/core/package.json`, `tsconfig.json` (root), `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
(verify only). No source `.ts` changes required.

## Rollback
Revert the `exports`/`customConditions` edits. Build core manually as a fallback
interim (NOT the chosen solution — it contradicts the "run from source" standard).

## Risks
- Custom-condition semantics differ between Bun and tsc; the probe above decides
  whether a separate `bun` condition is needed.
- If `types` points at `src/index.ts`, external consumers running `tsc` without
  the `development` condition still get `import: ./dist/index.js` + a `.d.ts`
  emitted by the build (`tsconfig.build.json` already emits `index.d.ts`).
  Confirm `dist/index.d.ts` is produced and shipped.

# Metascan v1.1 — Standards Conformance Remediation

## Goal
Close the three conformance gaps surfaced by the Architect validation of the
shipped v1, so the project passes its own enforcement gates (lint + typecheck +
test) from a clean checkout and matches the four locked standards exactly.

## Origin
Architect validation 2026-07-30. v1 plan
(`05d4dc81-7df1-4311-a98b-5570afefafbd`) is `done`; all 24 v1 tasks are `done`.
This plan is the remediation tail.

## Findings being remediated
1. **CRITICAL — Source resolution / CI red.** `@metascan/core` `exports` map
   only points at `./dist/*`, which is git-ignored and unbuildable in CI
   (no `build` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). `apps/server` consumes core
   via `workspace:*`, so from a clean clone `bun run typecheck` fails
   (TS2307 Cannot find module '@metascan/core') and the server test file errors
   out (84 tests → 83 pass / 1 fail / 1 error). Verified: building core makes
   `typecheck` clean and 96/96 tests pass. Governing standard:
   `0057ec32-0216-49ab-bf1b-c50370b730b4` (Runtime & Toolchain) — "apps run
   directly from source — no `dist/` required" + Enforcement/CI gate.
2. **MINOR — Non-HTML throws PARSE_ERROR.** `fetch.ts` returns `html: ""` for
   non-HTML content types; `preview.ts` then throws `PARSE_ERROR` (→ HTTP 502).
   Standard `e4c48c87-e4ef-4b91-9fad-98eedbdd80c1` (Fetch Safety) requires
   non-HTML to be skipped "without erroring (return empty fields)".
3. **MINOR — Adapter image URLs not absolute.** `adapters/youtube.ts` and
   `adapters/twitter.ts` return `og:image`/`twitter:image` raw. Standard
   `55d564d2-6fd1-4a7f-bb2d-a27a3b2aef37` (Output Contract) requires
   `image.url` to be absolute; Adapter Authoring checklist item 2
   (`cf5fd7c7-f7bf-4e1a-8499-96571d087d58`) requires "resolve all returned URLs
   to absolute (use the page base)".

## Affected surfaces
- `packages/core/package.json` (exports), shared/server tsconfig
  (`customConditions`), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (verify, no build needed).
- `packages/core/src/preview.ts` (non-HTML empty result), `fetch.ts`
  (contentType plumbing already present).
- `packages/core/src/adapters/youtube.ts`, `adapters/twitter.ts`, a shared
  URL-resolve util (refactor from `extractors/default.ts`), and the three
  colocated `*.test.ts`.

## Definition of done (v1.1)
- `bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun test` all green from a clean
  checkout with NO build step and NO `dist/`.
- Non-HTML responses return a 200 PreviewResult with empty title/description.
- Built-in adapters emit absolute `image.url` for relative OG/Twitter images.
- The four standards are unchanged; no new standard required.

## Risks
- Export-condition changes can affect the published `dist/` contract — must
  verify `bun pack` still resolves to `dist/` for external consumers.
- Custom-condition support differs between Bun and tsc; approach must work for
  both `bun test` and `tsc --noEmit`.

metadata.description: Bounds and error handling for fetching arbitrary user-supplied URLs. Basic SSRF posture per v1 decision.

content.text:
# Fetch Safety & Resilience

Applies to all outbound URL fetching in `@metascan/core`.

## v1 posture: BASIC (per product decision)
The server is assumed to run on a **trusted/internal** network for v1.
SSRF protections are intentionally minimal. **If the server becomes
internet-facing, this standard MUST be upgraded** to add destination IP
filtering (see "Upgrade path" below).

## Required guards (basic level)
- **Scheme allowlist:** only `http:` and `https:`. Reject everything else as `INVALID_URL`.
- **Per-request timeout:** default 1500 ms (configurable). Exceeding → `TIMEOUT`.
- **Redirect cap:** follow at most 3 redirects. Exceeding → `TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS`.
- **Response size cap:** read at most 2 MB of the body (configurable). Truncate parsing beyond that.
- **Graceful degradation:** network/HTTP failures → `FETCH_ERROR`; HTML parse failure → `PARSE_ERROR`. Never throw an untyped exception to the caller.
- **Never crashes the caller:** all public entry points either resolve a `PreviewResult` or throw a typed `PreviewError`.

## Resilience defaults
- Default `User-Agent` identifying metascan with a link to the repo.
- Accept `text/html` responses; skip clearly non-HTML content types without erroring (return empty fields).
- All timeouts/sizes/redirect limits configurable via `PreviewOptions` and (for the server) env vars.

## Upgrade path (when internet-facing)
Add a pre-fetch resolver step: resolve the hostname, reject if any resolved
address is private/loopback/link-local (RFC1918, 127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16,
::1, fc00::/7), then fetch. Re-evaluate DNS rebinding mitigation at the same
time. This is a known, documented risk for v1.

content.raw:
# Metascan Runtime & Toolchain

## Runtime
- **Primary runtime: Bun** (latest 1.2.x). Pin the exact version in the root
  `package.json` via `"packageManager"` (e.g. `"bun@1.3.14"`); document the
  floor (`>= 1.2.0`) in the README and each workspace's `"engines"`.
- Core (`@metascan/core`) is written against **web-standard APIs only**
  (global `fetch`, `URL`, `Request`, `Response`, `Headers`). Do not import
  `node:*` modules in core. This keeps core incidentally Node-18+ compatible
  while Bun remains the supported runtime and test target.
- The server (`apps/server`) is Bun-native: use `Bun.serve()` hosting a
  Hono app. It is an **internal app, not a published package** — it ships as
  the `metascan-server` bin and a Docker image.

## Monorepo layout
- Root `package.json` is `private: true` with
  `"workspaces": ["packages/*", "apps/*"]`.
- Two workspaces:
  - `packages/core` → published as `@metascan/core` (the engine + public API).
  - `apps/server` → **NOT published** (`"private": true`). Exposed as the
    `metascan-server` bin and as a Docker image; depends on core.
- Cross-package work: use `bun --filter '*' <script>` and
  `--parallel`/`--sequential` as needed.
- The server depends on core via a `"@metascan/core": "workspace:*"` entry.

## Language & types
- TypeScript, `strict: true`. `target: ESNext`, `module: ESNext`,
  `moduleResolution: Bundler`.
- All shared types live in `packages/core/src/types.ts` and are re-exported.
- Bun globals/types come from `@types/bun`; reference it via
  `"types": ["bun"]` in the tsconfig (NOT `"bun-types"` — that name does not
  resolve). Prefer explicit `import { test, expect } from "bun:test"` over
  global test functions.

## Testing
- Use the built-in **`bun:test`** runner
  (`import { test, expect, describe, beforeEach } from "bun:test"`).
- Colocate tests as `*.test.ts` next to the module under test.

## Build
- Build libraries with **`Bun.build`**: `format: "esm"`, `target: "bun"`,
  externalize peer/runtime deps, emit sourcemaps, output to `dist/`.
- Each published package declares `exports` (modern subpath exports),
  `types`, `main`/`module` pointing at `dist/`.
- Apps (`apps/server`) are run directly from source by Bun — no `dist/`
  required for the app itself (Docker bakes the source image).

## Lint/format
- Use **Biome** (fast, pairs well with Bun) for lint + format; single config
  `biome.json` at the repo root. No ESLint/Prettier.
- Biome default style: tabs + double quotes. Run `biome check .` for lint and
  `biome format --write .` to format.

## Enforcement
- **No `node:*` imports, project-wide.** Enforced by Biome `noRestrictedImports`
  (`style` group, `level: "error"`) with gitignore patterns `["node:*",
  "node:*/**"]` so both `node:fs` and `node:fs/promises` are caught. The server
  uses Bun globals (not Node built-ins), so this is safe everywhere; for
  `@metascan/core` it is what guarantees the library stays web-standard.
- **Core source is web-standard at compile time.** `packages/core/tsconfig.json`
  (the `src` config) sets `"types": []` and `"lib": ["ESNext", "WebWorker"]`
  and excludes `*.test.ts` — so core source may only use web globals (`fetch`,
  `URL`, `Request`, `Response`, `Headers`, …). A sibling
  `packages/core/tsconfig.test.json` adds `"types": ["bun"]` so tests can use
  `bun:test` and Bun globals.
- **CI gates.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
  followed by `lint` + `typecheck` + `test` on every push/PR to `main`. The CI
  Bun version MUST match the root `packageManager`.
- **Typecheck command.** `bun run typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` across all
  three configs (core src, core tests, server). Add new tsconfigs to this
  script when new workspaces are introduced.

## Do not
- Do not add Node-only APIs to core (e.g. `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:http`).
- Do not introduce a separate bundler (webpack/rollup/tsup) — use `Bun.build`.
- Do not pin exact patch versions of Bun in dependency ranges (engines floor
  only); the `packageManager` field is the one exact pin.
- Do not publish `apps/server` as an npm package.
